verses.sanskrit:
धृतराष्ट्र उवाच।
              अतितीव्राणि दुःखानि दुःसहानि बहूनि च । त्वत्तोऽहं सञ्जयाश्रौषं पुत्राणां चैव संक्षयम् ॥१॥
verses.english: Dhritarashtra said O Sanjaya, I have heard from you of great and intolerable grief's of fierce character as well as of the destruction of my sons.

verses.sanskrit: यथा त्वं मे कथयसे यथा युद्धमवर्तत । न सन्ति सूत कौरव्या इति मे निश्चिता मतिः ॥२॥
verses.english: O Suta (charioteer), from what you describe to me and also from how the battle was fought, my certain conclusion is that the Kauravas are not alive.

verses.sanskrit: दुर्योधनश्च विरथः कृतस्तत्र महारथः । धर्मपुत्रः कथं चक्रे तस्य वा नृपतिः कथम् ॥३॥
verses.english: In that fair battle, Duryodhana was deprived of his car. How did the son of Dharma fight; and how also did that prince (Duryodhana)?

verses.sanskrit: अपराह्णे कथं युद्धमभवल्लोमहर्षणम् । तन्ममाचक्ष्व तत्त्वेन कुशलो ह्यसि सञ्जय ॥४॥
verses.english: How did take place the battle, that made the hairs to stand on points, in the afternoon? O Sanjaya, relate to me all these in detail; for you are an expert in this
verses.bhavadeepa: विरथः कृत इत्युक्तं तत्र युद्धे धर्मपुत्रः कथं तं विरथं चक्रे तस्य तं च नृपतिर्दुर्योधनः कथमयुद्ध्यत इति शेषः ॥३॥

verses.sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच।
              संसक्तेषु तु सैन्येषु वध्यमानेषु भागशः । रथमन्यं समास्थाय पुत्रस्तव विशांपते ॥५॥
verses.english: Sanjaya said While the soldiers on both sides were thus engaged in fighting in their respective divisions your son, king Duryodhana, O lord of earth, ascending upon another car and being filled with great wrath, like a snake possessing virulent poison, addressed his charioteer, saying-

verses.sanskrit: क्रोधेन महता युक्तः सविषो भुजगो यथा । दुर्योधनः समालक्ष्य धर्मराजं युधिष्ठिरम् ॥६॥
प्रोवाच सूतं त्वरितो याहि याहीति भारत । तत्र मां प्रापय क्षिप्रं सारथे यत्र पाण्डवः ॥७॥
verses.english: Do you proceed, do you proceed, quickly. After he, O descendant of the Bharata race, had beheld Yudhishthira, the king of righteousness, he said-"O charioteer, most speedily do you lead me to that place, where the royal son of Pandu, having been clad in armour, looks most resplendent with the umbrella held over his head."

verses.sanskrit: ध्रियमाणातपत्रेण राजा राजति दंशितः । स सूतश्चोदितो राज्ञा राज्ञः स्यन्दनमुत्तमम् ॥८॥
युधिष्ठिरस्याभिमुखं प्रेषयामास संयुगे । ततो युधिष्ठिरः क्रुद्धः प्रभिन्न इव कुञ्जरः ॥९॥
verses.english: Then the charioteer, being thus urged by the king, led the foremost of cars belonging to the king to the presence of king Yudhishthira in the battle. were an

verses.sanskrit: सारथिं चोदयामास याहि यत्र सुयोधनः । तौ समाजग्मतुर्वीरौ भ्रातरौ रथसत्तमौ ॥१०॥
verses.english: Thereupon Yudhishthira, being filled with wrath and resembling an infuriate elephant, urged his charioteer, asking him to proceed to the place, where Suyodhana took his stand.

verses.sanskrit: समेत्य च महावीरौ संरब्धौ युद्धदुर्मदौ । ववर्षतुर्महेष्वासौ शरैरन्योन्यमाहवे ॥११॥
verses.english: Those two heroic warriors, who were brothers to each other and who were the best of car-warriors and who were possessed of immense prowess and who also invincible in battle, coming in contact with each other, engaged themselves in encounter. Moreover these two mighty bowmen began to strike each other with numerous shafts in that battle.

verses.sanskrit: ततो दुर्योधनो राजा धर्मशीलस्य मारिष । शिलाशितेन भल्लेन धनुश्चिच्छेद संयुगे ॥१२॥
verses.english: Thereupon, O sire, the king Duryodhana severed the bow of that righteous one (Yudhishthira) by means of a broad-headed arrows, sharpened on a stone, in the battle.

verses.sanskrit: तं नामृष्यत संक्रुद्धो ह्यवमानं युधिष्ठिरः । अपविध्य धनुश्छिन्नं क्रोधसंरक्तलोचनः ॥१३॥
verses.english: Yudhishthira, who became highly enraged, did not indeed, car that insult. Then the son of Dharma, whose eyes became red with wrath, throwing aside his severed bow and grasping another bow, stood at the head of his army and cut-off the standard and bow of Duryodhana.

verses.sanskrit: अन्यत्कार्मुकमादाय धर्मपुत्रश्चमूमुखे । दुर्योधनस्य चिच्छेद ध्वजं कार्मुकमेव च ॥१४॥
अथान्यद्धनुरादाय प्राविध्यत युधिष्ठिरम् । तावन्योन्यं सुसंक्रुद्धौ शस्त्रवर्षाण्यमुञ्चताम् ॥१५॥
verses.english: Then, having taken up another bow, he (Duryodhana) pierced the son of Pandu in return. Those two heroic warriors, poured forth showers of arrows upon each other.

verses.sanskrit: सिंहाविव सुसंरब्धौ परस्परजिगीषया । जघ्नतुस्तौ रणेऽन्योन्यं नर्दमानौ वृषाविव ॥१६॥
verses.english: Who like two lions filled with great rage, were highly enraged and who also were most desirous of defeating each other in the battle, those two most powerful car-warriors smote down each other like two roaring bulls.

verses.sanskrit: अन्तरं मार्गमाणौ च चेरतुस्तौ महारथौ । ततः पूर्णायतोत्सृष्टैः शरैस्तौ तु कृतव्रणौ ॥१७॥
verses.english: In the battle, and also they wandered over the field, expecting to catch each other on their weak points. Thereupon the two heroes, who were wounded by the arrows shot from bows stretched to their fullest length, looked most handsome, O great monarch, resembling two flowering Kinshukas.

verses.sanskrit: विरेजतुर्महाराज किंशुकाविव पुष्पितौ । ततो राजन्विमुञ्चन्तौ सिंहनादान्मुहुर्मुहुः ॥१८॥
तलयोश्च तथा शब्दान् धनुषश्च महाहवे । शङ्खशब्दवरांश्चैव चक्रतुस्तौ नरेश्वरौ ॥१९॥
verses.english: Then, O monarch, those two rulers of men uttered roars of a lion in order to terrify each other; as also they made sounds with their palms and with their bows; and again, sent forth the loudest sound with their conches in that dreadful battle.

verses.sanskrit: अन्योन्यं तौ महाराज पीडयाञ्चक्रतुर्भृशम् । ततो युधिष्ठिरो राजा पुत्रं तव शरैस्त्रिभिः ॥२०॥
verses.english: O great king, those two oppressed each other very greatly. Thereupon king Yudhishthira, who became very angry, struck your son on the chest with arrows, that were very irresistible, having had the impetuosity of thunder.

verses.sanskrit: आजघानोरसि क्रुद्धो वज्रवेगैर्दुरासदैः । प्रतिविव्याध तं तूर्णं तव पुत्रो महीपतिः ॥२१॥
पञ्चभिर्निशितैर्बाणैः स्वर्णपुङ्खैः शिलाशितैः । ततो दुर्योधनो राजा शक्तिं चिक्षेप भारत ॥२२॥
verses.english: Your son, that ruler of earth, most quickly pierced him (Yudhishthira) in return with five keen arrows, that were equipt with the wings of gold and sharpened on a stone.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वपारसवीं तीक्ष्णां महोल्काप्रतिमां तदा । तामापतन्तीं सहसा धर्मराजः शितैः शरैः ॥२३॥
verses.english: Thereupon, O descendant of the Bharata race, the king Duryodhana shot an arrows, called Sakti, that was capable of slaughtering all creatures and was sharp-edged and also that looked like a large, resplendent brand.

verses.sanskrit: त्रिभिश्चिच्छेद सहसा तं च विव्याध पञ्चभिः । निपपात ततः साऽथ स्वर्णदण्डा महास्वना ॥२४॥
verses.english: Then the king of righteousness (Yudhishthira) severed into three fragments that arrows, which coursed towards him suddenly by means of numerous sharp shafts; and again, he, all on a sudden, pierced the prince himself (Duryodhana) with five others.
verses.bhavadeepa: सर्वपारसवीं सर्वविनाशिनीं गौरादिः । ‘तिरस्कारविनाशे च पुंसि पारसवः पुमान्’ इति मेदिनी ॥२३॥

verses.sanskrit: निपतन्ती महोल्केव व्यराजच्छिखिसन्निभा । शक्तिं विनिहतां दृष्ट्वा पुत्रस्तव विशांपते ॥२५॥
verses.english: Thereupon that arrow, which was furnished with a golden staff and that was capable of producing a lould whizz, dropped down (upon the ground); and its falling, like a great brand attended with the blazing flames, looked most resplendent.

verses.sanskrit: नवभिर्निशितैर्भल्लैर्निजघान युधिष्ठिरम् । सोऽतिविद्धो बलवता शत्रुणा शत्रुतापनः ॥२६॥
verses.english: O ruler of earth, your son, beholding that Shakti-arrow thus severed into pieces, struck Yudhishthira with nine whetted and sharppointed arrows.

verses.sanskrit: दुर्योधनं समुद्दिश्य बाणं जग्राह सत्वरः । समाधत्त च तं बाणं धनुर्मध्ये महाबलः ॥२७॥
verses.english: That scorcher of antagonists, being thus deeply penetrated by the most powerful enemy, quickly equipped himself and took up an arrow, aiming at Duryodhana.

verses.sanskrit: चिक्षेप च महाराज ततः क्रुद्धः पराक्रमी । स तु बाणः समासाद्य तव पुत्रं महारथम् ॥२८॥
verses.english: O mighty monarch, thereupon that hero, possessed of immense strength and great powers, being greatly wrathful, put that arrow upon his bow-string and directed it (at his antagonist). Indeed, that arrow, approaching towards your son, that powerful car-warrior stupefied that prince and then went down the earth.

verses.sanskrit: व्यामोहयत राजानं धरणीं च ददार ह । ततो दुर्योधनः क्रुद्धो गदामुद्यम्य वेगितः ॥२९॥
विधित्सुः कलहस्यान्तं धर्मराजमुपाद्रवत् । तमुद्यतगदं दृष्ट्वा दण्डहस्तमिवान्तकम् ॥३०॥
verses.english: Thereupon Duryodhana, who was filled with wrath, most quickly raising his mace, afflicted the king of righteousness (Yudhishthira) with the desire of piercing him through, in order to put an end to all hostilities (between the Kurus Pandavas).

verses.sanskrit: धर्मराजो महाशक्तिं प्राहिणोत्तव सूनवे । दीप्यमानां महावेगां महोल्कां ज्वलितामिव ॥३१॥
verses.english: Beholding him thus raising his mace like Death himself armed with his rod, the king of righteousness (Yudhishthira) shot that mighty Shakti-arrow at your son, that blazed forth most brilliantly and was endued with great impetuosity and also that resembled a large and resplendent brand

verses.sanskrit: रथस्थः स तया विद्धो वर्म भित्त्वा स्तनान्तरे । भृशं संविग्नहृदयः पपात च मुमोह च ॥३२॥
verses.english: Then he (the Kuru prince), who stayed on his car, having been pierced on the chest by that arrow, first piercing his vitals and also having been greatly pained a heart, fell down and became senseless.

verses.sanskrit: भीमस्तमाह च ततः प्रतिज्ञामनुचिन्तयन् । नायं वध्यस्तव नृप इत्युक्तः स न्यवर्तत ॥३३॥
verses.english: Thereupon Bhima, recollecting his own vow, uttered these words 'O prince, (Yudhishthira), this one is not to be slaughtered by you.' Being thus addressed Yudhishthira abstained (from slaying him).

verses.sanskrit: ततस्त्वरितमागम्य कृतवर्मा तवात्मजम् । प्रत्यपद्यत राजानं निमग्नं व्यसनार्णवे ॥३४॥
verses.english: Thereupon Kritavarman, most quickly approaching towards your son, got near that prince, who was then drowned in the great ocean of calamity.

verses.sanskrit: गदामादाय भीमोऽपि हेमपट्टपरिष्कृताम् । अभिदुद्राव वेगेन कृतवर्माणमाहवे ॥३५॥
verses.english: Then Bhima, too, grasping his mace, that was equipt with gold and flaxen chords, proceeded with great violence against Kritavarman in that dreadful battle.

verses.sanskrit: एवं तदद्भवद्युद्धं त्वदीयानां परैः सह । अपराह्णे महाराज काङ्क्षतां विजयं युधि ॥३६॥
verses.english: O great king, thus took place the battle between the forces on your side and their antagonists, in that afternoon while the parties were most desirous of victory in the battle.
